messages:
Alex S.: FYI customer ACME is seeing intermittent 503s + p95 tail latency spikes on hosted inference since ~09:30 UTC. They say it correlates with large batched requests from their ingestion job.
Priya (support): Logged with customer, asked for SDK version, sample payload, and a trace-id. Customer sent back SDK v1.3.7, using batch size 64 for embeddings, and one trace-id: trace_0a9f8c. They also attached a short curl repro.
acme-sre: Here is minimal repro we saw (sanitized):

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","inputs":["... repeated 64 items ..."]}'

acme-sre: When we run in a loop we start getting 503s and then client-side timeouts after a few minutes. Backoff doesn't help; it looks like a gateway-level queue building up.
Ingrid (oncall): Thanks, will take lead. Can you paste the trace-id logs and the gateway request_id from the curl response? Also which region?
Priya (support): Region: eu-west1. Customer provided the API response snippet: {"error":{"type":"gateway_error","message":"service_unavailable","request_id":"rq_7f3b2e"}}
Josh (runtime): Initial look: gateway returned 503s while downstream model pods were still healthy. Suspect inflight queueing + worker saturation on the edge proxy. Need p95 latency histograms and kvcache stats for that time window.
Josh (runtime): Quick mitigation: ask customer to temporarily reduce batch size to 16 and add client-side concurrency cap (max 4 inflight). Also set per-request timeout to 60s instead of default. That should avoid the retry-fanout.
Alex S.: Communicated mitigations to customer with sample SDK patch: 

// pseudo-code for node SDK
const client = new RedwoodClient({timeout: 60000, maxInflight: 4});
await client.embeddings.create({model: 'embed-large', inputs: chunk(inputs, 16)});

Priya (support): Customer tried reducing batch to 16 and concurrency to 3 — 503 rate dropped by ~90% in their test run. They want a root cause and a permanent fix.
Ingrid (oncall): Recording next steps:
- Collect gateway proxy metrics (queue length, accept rate) for eu-west1 09:20-09:45 UTC
- Pull model pod metrics (GPU utilization, process_cpu) same window
- Get kvcache hit/miss and lock contention events
- Check recent deploys to gateway/orchestrator around 09:15 UTC

Josh (runtime): I see a small config change rolled to gateway at 09:14 that increased max_inflight_queue from 1024 -> 2048 to improve throughput. That likely allowed more inflight requests to pile up and then the gateway hit a soft limit, causing 503s under burst. We'll roll back that change and add a safer backpressure threshold.
deploy-bot: deploy roll-back started by Ingrid — gateway-config rollback to previous(2026-02-18T09:10:12Z).
deploy-bot: rollback successful in eu-west1 (3/3 pods).
Ingrid (oncall): After rollback, monitoring shows p95 latency returned to baseline and 503s stopped. Need to schedule a config tuned rollout and add telemetry alert for queue growth.
Alex S.: Shared rollback and customer mitigation update with ACME and recommended long-term steps (smaller batch defaults, SDK concurrency knob, gateway backpressure). Customer asked for ETA to get a permanent config with throttling by tenant.
Josh (runtime): I'll prepare a tenant-aware throttling RFC and a short patch for gateway to cap queue depth per-tenant + early 429s instead of letting 503s cascade. Target: proposal by EOD tomorrow, patch + canary next week.
acme-sre: Thanks for the fast rollback and the mitigation suggestions — we'll keep batch size lowered for now and wait for your patch. Please ping when the canary is up so we can test. :thumbsup:
Priya (support): Noted. I'll follow up with scheduled customer test window next week. Closing this thread when RFC lands.
